problem: In a class, $17$ students are boys, and $23$ are girls. Of the boys, $2$ belong to the school chess club. Of the girls, $3$ are in the chess club. What is the probability that a randomly selected student in the class is in the chess club?

feedback.problem: In a class, $20$ students are boys, and $24$ are girls. $5%$ of the boys are engaged in a sports section, and $25%$ of the girls are engaged in a sports section. What is the probability that a randomly selected student is engaged in a sports section?
feedback.worked_solution:
Let $S$ be the event that the selected student is engaged in a sports section, and let $B$ be the event that the student is a boy. Then ${B}^{′}$ is the event that the student is a girl.

To calculate the probability that a randomly selected student is engaged in a sports section, we can use the law of total probability:

$$
P(S)=P(S\cap B)+P(S\cap {B}^{′})
$$

There are $20$ boys in the class, and $5%$ of them are engaged in a sports section. So, the number of boys engaged in a sports section is

$$
\frac{5}{100}\cdot 20=1.
$$

There are $24$  girls in the class, and $25%$ of them are engaged in a sports section. So, the number of girls  engaged in a sports section is

$$
\frac{25}{100}\cdot 24=6.
$$

To calculate $P(S\cap B),$ we take the number of boys engaged in a sports section $(1)$ and divide it by the total number of students in the class $(20+24=44).$ So, we have

$$
P(S\cap B)=\frac{1}{44}.
$$

Similarly, to calculate $P(S\cap {B}^{′}),$ we take the number of girls engaged in a sports section $(6)$ and divide it by the total number of students in the class $(44).$ So, we have

$$
P(S\cap {B}^{′})=\frac{6}{44}.
$$

Finally, substituting the above information into the law of total probability, the probability that a randomly selected student is engaged in a sports section is

$$
\begin{aligned}P(S) & =P(S\cap B)+P(S\cap {B}^{′}) \\  & =\frac{1}{44}+\frac{6}{44} \\  & =\frac{7}{44}.\end{aligned}
$$
